title: Thu 12 Nov: Foreign money lifts Nifty to nine-month high
description:
Hot topic: foreign money pushed the Nifty to a nine-month high, but Gift Nifty points lower after an overnight Nvidia shock, with India's inflation print due today. Then: banks, Tata Power, the rupee, oil, US yields, IT, CPI, IndiGo and gold.

1. Nifty climbs 0.84% to 25,255, a nine-month high, as November foreign buying tops 5.6 billion dollars (Upstox; Business Standard)
2. Nifty Bank rises 1.76% to 60,792 as PSU lenders jump 2.9% for a third day of bank leadership (Liquide; Upstox)
3. Tata Power's September-quarter profit rises 49% to 1,366 crore rupees as revenue climbs 26% (Upstox; Free Press Journal)
4. Rupee firms to 93.69 per dollar, its strongest since April, on foreign equity inflows (Business Today)
5. Brent rebounds to about 93 dollars as Hormuz tanker attacks continue; Goldman lifts its December forecast to 105 dollars (Business Recorder; HDFC Sky)
6. US 10-year yield returns to 5% after hotter October inflation and Waller's hawkish comments (CBS News; Saxo)
7. IT stocks lag again as Nifty IT slips 0.5% while banks and autos rally (Liquide; Yahoo Finance)
8. India's October inflation, due today, is expected near 6%, the top of the RBI's band (Business Today; Mint via TradingView)
9. IndiGo jumps 4.3% to 5,665 rupees as airlines rally on the dip in crude (Business Standard; Kotak Neo)
10. Gold slips below 4,000 dollars an ounce after the hot US inflation print (Kitco; Investing.com)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated from the hosts' own recordings. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm Pri.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm SU. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Today's big one: foreign money pushed the Nifty to a nine-month high. But Gift Nifty points lower this morning.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: SU, what happened on Wednesday?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty rose 0.84%, or 210.40 points, to 25,255.05. The Sensex gained 0.95% to 81,879.40.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Intraday, the Nifty touched 25,424.35, its highest in about nine months. Breadth was strong, with 2,495 stocks up and 1,166 down.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And the money behind it?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign investors bought a provisional 12,563 crore rupees, while domestic funds sold 8,434 crore. November foreign buying is now 65,735 crore rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's more than 5.6 billion dollars in under two weeks.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Who moved the market?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: PSU banks led the gains, and M&M was the Nifty's top gainer as autos rose 2.1%. ICICI Bank fell 1.1% against the rally.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Why should India care, if Gift Nifty is already pointing down?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. This rally runs on foreign money. Today's open tests whether that flow survives an overnight Nvidia shock and India's inflation print.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Gift Nifty was at 25,189, down 0.14%, late on Wednesday. Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.9% early Thursday after the Nvidia report.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what should I watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Whether the Nifty holds above 25,200 and foreign buying continues in Thursday's provisional data. A hot CPI and foreign selling could push it below 25,000.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, SBI, M&M and ICICI Bank. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: banks lead for a third straight session.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty Bank rose 1.76% to 60,792.40, and reclaimed 61,000 intraday, a nine-month high near its record.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The PSU Bank index jumped 2.94% to 9,167.20, and private banks rose 1.14%. ICICI Bank fell 1.1% to 1,571.60 rupees.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: banks are where foreign buyers are putting money, so they set the index's direction. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: SBI, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, PNB.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: Tata Power's profit jumps 49%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Profit rose 48.6% to 1,366 crore rupees in July to September. Revenue rose 26.3% to 19,636 crore rupees.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Sounds great. What's the catch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Margins. EBITDA rose 11%, but the margin fell to 18.7% from 21.2% as fuel costs more than tripled.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The board also approved 11,871 crore rupees for an 1,800 megawatt pumped-storage project. The auditor flagged an arbitration award the company is challenging.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a record profit now meets heavy spending and a thinner margin. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Tata Power, NTPC, Adani Power, Power Grid.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: the rupee hits its strongest level since April.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The rupee closed at about 93.69 per dollar, up about 0.26%. That's more than 3.3% above its record low of 96.96 in May.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign investors have bought about 6.4 billion dollars of Indian shares in November, the most in a month since September 2024.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Is the rupee worry over, then?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Not quite. The dollar index hit its highest since May 2025, and Axis Bank still sees the rupee at 100 by June 2027.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a firmer rupee cuts imported inflation and helps oil importers. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: IndiGo, Infosys, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: oil bounces back.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Brent settled at 92.76 dollars, up 1.4%, after hitting 89.16 dollars on Tuesday, its lowest since August. In Asia on Thursday it was about 91.74 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: About 37 vessels were attacked near Hormuz in October, and Goldman raised its December Brent forecast to 105 dollars from 90.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: every 10 dollars on Brent moves India's import bill, the rupee and oil marketers' margins. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: ONGC, BPCL, HPCL, IOC.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: the US 10-year yield is back at 5%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US October inflation rose 0.4% on the month, against 0.3% expected. Core inflation rose 0.3%, against 0.2%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Fed Governor Waller said a December hike looks likely. The 10-year was about 4.99% in Asian trade, with about 85% odds priced for a December hike.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a 5% US yield raises the bar for foreign money in emerging markets like India. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, HDFC Bank.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: IT stocks miss the party again.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nifty IT fell 0.53% to 32,295.60, with Tech Mahindra down 0.91% and HCLTech 0.85%, while banks and autos rallied.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And what's this Nvidia news?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Nvidia fell about 7 to 8% after hours on a report its board may oust Jensen Huang. That came after the Nasdaq rose 1.6%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: IT is funding the rotation into banks, and a US tech shock can deepen the lag. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Infosys, TCS, HCLTech, Tech Mahindra.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: India's inflation number lands today.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: October CPI is due today. Economists polled by Informist and Mint expect 6%, and Bloomberg Economics 6.1%, against 5.54% in September.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: ICRA expects food inflation above 8%, and IDFC First expects a 25 basis point RBI hike in December.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a print at 6% or above hits the top of the RBI's band and lifts hike odds. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: DLF, Godrej Properties, Lodha, Bajaj Finance.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: airlines take off on cheaper crude.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: IndiGo rose 4.33% to 5,665 rupees, and is up 16.1% since 30 October, as Brent fell from above 100 dollars to the low 90s.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So fuel bills are already lower?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Not yet. Jet fuel prices are revised periodically and depend on the rupee, so cheaper crude reaches airlines only with a lag.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: airline shares are pricing in fuel relief that hasn't shown up in jet fuel prices yet. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: IndiGo.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And story ten: gold slips below 4,000 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Spot gold fell more than 1% to about 3,987 dollars an ounce, as the hot US inflation print fuelled bets on bigger Fed hikes.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: In India, MCX gold futures still rose 0.47% as the rupee firmed, and silver gained 2.2%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: gold below 4,000 dollars eases costs for Indian jewellers, but signals tighter global money. Sentiment: mixed. Stocks in focus: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Muthoot Finance.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch today: India's October inflation print, and whether foreign buyers keep coming after the Nvidia shock.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
